notes.title: Early look at new in-built Map Editor...
notes.content:
As part of the bid to get adlengine out of early access we're working on an official in-built suite of tools to aid development using #adlengine in-line with bringing it to a more learnable state.

Starting with a dedicated map editor which will allow you to quickly lay down the foundations of any scenario / game.

[i][b]Below is a sneak peak.[/b][/i]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29210544/9bf2969901e8ffdfdd2c2a3091e18ce392338bde.gif[/img]

From this editor you will be able to add / delete / edit rooms and any contents within them, such as exits, objects, characters and more.

[h1]Other tools we'll be developing as part of the suite:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Script editor that will make complex scripting easier.
[*] UI editor to allow you to customise or totally alter the look and experience.
[/list]

[h1]Future tools:[/h1]

Timeline editor to handle events and dialogue manager.

notes.title: ADLENGINE v1.1.61.5d
notes.content:
[h1]Major changes are afoot.[/h1]


[h1]Rendering Text Changes[/h1]
Rendering text is now handled using text areas instead of static text objects, which will soon be added to theme controls, these allow for greater control of text, neater rendering and the ability to scroll back through previous text that has been rendered.
Hoping these will also be more friendlier to screen readers (confirmed working with NVDA screen reader).


[h1]New friendlier commands in this version:[/h1]

New IS command, a there and then or staggered comparison command. Alternative to the IF command which stores comparison commands which are called when you type specific phrases.

[list]
[*] is something
[*] equal to something
[*] not equal to something
[*] greater than something
[*] less than something
[*] or equal to something (may just become or equal to)
[*] then do something
[*] and do something
[*] and2 do something
[*] and3 do something
[*] else do something
[*] end is / endis / end
[/list]

An example of this in use:

[list]
[*] #haskey=0
[*] is haskey
[*] equal to 1
[*] then unlockdoor()
[*] else narrate need to find a key.
[/list]

[h1]Changes to delete commands.[/h1]
[list]
[*] delete object objectname
[*] delete script scriptname
[*] delete var variablename
[*] delete custom customname
[/list]
​

[h1]More great stuff to come.[/h1]

Editing Map Data Direct
map data | will be changed to / allowing you to write directly to the data i.e.

Existing data...

/entityname/health/100
or /x/y/z/objectname/open/y
Or writing new data.

[h1]Official Choose Your Path Mod[/h1]

The options mod allows you to render buttons as major choices, usable to either handle choices in game or could be used for dialogue. See the manual for commands related to this.

notes.title: In the meantime...
notes.content:
Whilst we're busy rewriting adlengine...

I will continue to work on the original Adliberum Engine and aim to get it out of Steam Early Access in 2019.

Notably: emphasis will be placed on locking down the core elements, providing a friendlier experience with menus etc, better documentation and in-built tutorials, more support for languages and some example games to download.

For now though, happy holidays. Catch you all in 2019!

notes.title: The future of Adliberum Engine
notes.content:
Apologies for the really long period of down time, life unfortunately has a real nasty habit of getting in the way at times. Looking forward to a kinder, more productive 2019.

Plus with the original software I used to create it no longer being updated and the knock on effect is that it's going to need a full rewrite.

I'm not able to just simply convert adlengine because of its complexity, so I have slowly been recreating the engine entirely in Construct 3. Which will become adlengine 2.

The engine will to the most part mirror across, and I will do my best to ensure the map files etc don't change (too much). Worse case I'll write an editor to convert the maps over to the new format.

I will be placing a lot more emphasis on the learning side of it, plus will be working hard to ensure it has some example games to play / edit.

Thank you for your support.

Here's a brief snapshot of the new engine so far..

notes.title: 1.1.60.7 - CYOA / THEME / ADVANCED FILTER COMMANDS
notes.content:
[h1]Updates in 1.1.60.7[/h1]

[h1]// NEW CHOOSE YOUR ADVENTURE FUNCTIONALITY //[/h1]

You enable CYOA mode per room. Which gives 1-4 choice buttons.

[code]room is cyoa[/code]

You can turn on / off choices using

[code]cyoa 1 is on / off[/code]
[code]cyoa 2 is on / off[/code]
[code]cyoa 3 is on / off[/code]
[code]cyoa 4 is on / off[/code]

To set the text of a choice;

[code]1 is ...[/code]
[code]2 is ...[/code]
[code]3 is ...[/code]
[code]4 is ...[/code]

When you set the text it will default the command to the same as you wrote for the text, for example take dirt, would run the command take dirt.

To manually set what command a choice calls;

[code]1 does ... [/code]
[code]2 does ... [/code]
[code]3 does ... [/code]
[code]4 does ... [/code]

They can be used to call single commands OR run scripts using;
[code]do ... [/code]


// NEW ON-START SCRIPT //

If script on-start is found it will be run AFTER the level has loaded. Create this script using the in-built editor;

[code]editor[/code]

[h1]// THEME EDITING / MANIPULATION //[/h1]

All major theme elements can be edited now. To list them use;

[code]listui[/code]

You can then edit / delete any theme element listed: i.e.

[code]{text-debug}.delete
{image-main}.width=800
{image-main}.width=600[/code]

etc


[h1]// ADVANCED SCRIPTING //[/h1]


Added new commands to fetch / filter data.

[code]fetchlocal ____
fetchglobal ____
fetchprivate _____[/code]

The fetch commands grab all data matching your query preparing it for filtering.

Use the filter commands to prepare data for filtering.

[code]filterlocal ____
filterglobal ____
filterprivate ____[/code]

Once you have the filtered data you can then use the strip command to keep what you want, please note  the aim is to finish up with a single piece of data. You will get a warning if you have no results OR too results are too broad.

[code]keep ____[/code]

e.g.

[code]fetchlocal box
filterlocal box
keep -islocked[/code]

This will return the key ie. '0|0|0|obj-box-islocked' and the value ie 'y'

You can then access this data with the following %special%.

[code]%SYS[FILTERKEY] for the kept key[/code]
[code]%SYS[FILTERVALUE] for the kept value[/code]

notes.title: 1.1.60.6 - NEW ACCESSIBILITY COMMANDS + SCREEN READER
notes.content:
In this version we have enabled a tonne of accessibility functions. Made minor improvements to the inbuilt editor.

[h1]NEW ACCESSIBILITY COMMANDS:[/h1]

Activate accessibility input box.

[code]input on/off[/code]

[h1]customise input box colors.[/h1]

[code]input b&w
input w&b
input red
input blue
input green
input white
input black[/code]

[h1]customise input box font size.[/h1]

[code]input small
input medium
input large[/code]

[h1]NEW SCREEN READER FUNCTIONALITY:[/h1]

Activate screen reader mode (should work with NVDA as it triggers NVDA via alert boxes) - this also activates the accessible input box.

[code]reader on/off[/code]
enter will move to the next queued speech

[h1]OTHER ACCESSIBILITY COMMANDS:[/h1]

[code]speech on/off
voices = lists all available speech synthesis voices.
voice is [1-X] = sets the voice based on the number specified (use the voices command to get a list!)
pause / p = pauses speech synthesis
play = resumes speech synthesis
[/code]

notes.title: NEW VERSION: 1.1.60.1 | All New Power Commands Added (nb: steam overlay = broken)
notes.content:
IMPORTANT: steam overlay IS currently not working with the new update.

UPDATE NOTES: 1.1.60.1

-----------------------------------------------------------
AUTO ADD TO INTELLISENSE
-----------------------------------------------------------

1. certain commands will now automatically add items to intellisense now, e.g. obj is takeable would add take obj to intellisense.

-----------------------------------------------------------
ENTER / EXIT TRIGGERS SCRIPT
-----------------------------------------------------------

2. on-enter & on-exit triggers now in place, it will look for a script based on the direction they enter / leave and run it if present; i.e. on-exit-e OR on-enter-se.

-----------------------------------------------------------
GLOBAL ACCESS TO DATA
-----------------------------------------------------------

3. you can now get global access to anything to amend / update data etc by using;

> entity\param\value
> room\param\value

i.e. box\isvisible\n
i.e. dungeon\name\dingy dungeon

------------------------------------------------------------------
RUN COMMANDS FROM ANOTHER LOCATION
------------------------------------------------------------------

4. you can now run select commands remotely.

> select entity/roomname/or?
> build box
> deselect

-------------------------------------------------------------------
REPLACE COMMAND
-------------------------------------------------------------------

5. replace commands can be used to replace any string or number or combination of from all data sources (USE with caution)

> replaceall this&that
> replacekey this&that
> replacevalue this&that

-------------------------------------------------------------------
WRITE DIRECT TO SCRIPT
-------------------------------------------------------------------

6. writescript commands that allow scripts to be constructed manually via scripting

> writescript scriptname

> writelocal towrite; (always terminate with ;) - writes data to local script
> writeglobal towrite
> writeprivate towrite

> clearlocal scriptname - clears a local script of any data (retains key)
> clearglobal scriptname
> clearprivate scriptname

> dellocal scriptname - deletes local script data
> delglobal scriptname
> delprivate scriptname

----------------------------------------------------------------
FETCH COMMAND/S
----------------------------------------------------------------

7. new fetch commands allow you to grab any data based on search params! the result values will be stored as follows;

SYS[FETCH-COUNT] - number of results matched.
SYS[FETCHX] i.e. 1-x

> fetchlocal x
> fetchglobal y
> fetchprivate z

Once fetched, you can then use SYS[FETCH] to use the found data.

i.e. room name is %SYS[FETCH]%

-----------------------------------------------------------------

I will also be working on a tutorial map that will help demonstrate adliberum engine's plethora of commands.

~ Liam

notes.title: ADLENGINE BUILD 1.1.55.5... NOW LIVE! (REPEAT, DUPLICATE OBJECTS, ASSIGN CLASSES & MORE)
notes.content:
[h1]NEW: REPEAT COMMAND:[/h1]

[code]
repeat:narrate boo;
repeat 10;
[/code]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29210544/4bfd03fc0e732c30b07551b4d56145cc6079dac2.gif[/img]
_____________________________

[h1]NEW: SYS VARS:[/h1]

SYS:CHOSEN (result from choose command)
SYS:ROLLED (result from rolled dice random comand)
SYS:LOOPINDEX (the position in the for loop command)
SYS:TARGET (from target, hit, attack and focus commands - also when assigning a class to an entity)

To use you can recall as a special lookup %SYS:TARGET%.
_____________________________

[h1]NEW: ASSIGN COMMAND[/h1]
Instead of assigning classes on build, you now assign classes post build. i.e.
[code]
build map
map.obj (assigns the obj class - classes are stored as global scripts! - ignore store as .class option)
[/code]

[b]Example: BOOK CLASS.[/b]
[code]
%target% is takeable;
%target% is readable;
[/code]

Then you would type:
[code]
map.book
[/code]
_____________________________

[h1]SCRIPTING: USE ! TO FORCE FEEDBACK ON COMMANDS[/h1]
[code]
!%target% is takeable;
[/code]

This will force the engine to tell the player that the targeted object is now takeable.
_____________________________

[h1]||%SEP%||%A%||%RATE%||[/h1]

You can now put special lookup commands next to each other by separating using || as above.
_____________________________

[h1]UPDATE: %SPECIAL% also looks in SESSION DATA[/h1]
type showdata to see all map data to see what you have access to, for example:
[code]
?%n-is-active%=1:narrate open!narrate closed;
[/code]
_____________________________

[h1]UPDATE: DUPLICATE OBJECTS[/h1]
IF you build more than one of the same object it will create duplicates with a number appended to the end. i.e. map, map2, map3 etc..
_____________________________

[h1]DELETE[/h1]
Now automatically detects what you are trying to delete including objects, scripts, variables and custom commands.
_____________________________

[h1]FIXES:[/h1]

FIXED: store as global IF (AND)
FIXED: store as local IF (THEN)

notes.content:
Lots of cool new stuff in this build.

[h1]WHICH.. IS (select case)[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29210544/2ca50335534003f9c2d02fcb35db2ccfd053b0e4.gif[/img]

[how to use] first add IS statements by doing the following
[code]isXYZ:do something[/code]

IS accepts boolean 0-1, true/false, numbers  0-9, y/n or can also accept custom naming.

e.g.

[code]is0:room is dark
is1:room is light[/code]

or..

[code]isneg:narrate -1
isneutral:narrate 0
ispos: narrate 1
[/code]

To run a WHICH check:
[code]which %cranelever%[/code]


[h1]FOR LOOPS[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29210544/d48e9cec2dfd1401bcb93be959bf741e563de7ce.gif[/img]

FOR loops allow you to loop a task X amount of times.

e.g.

To set a FOR LOOP:
[code]
for:do testscript
[/code]

To run a FOR LOOP:
[code]
for 0-10
[/code]

Example Script Content To Run:
[code]
testscript:
narrate %x%;
~x+1
[/code]

Where x in my example are array entries containing simple map data 0/1s


[h1]ARRAYS[/h1]

Array like data can be defined using variables. For example:

[code]
#map[0]=0
#map[1]=1
#map[2]=0

#map[0][0]=1
#map[1][0]=0
#map[2][0]=1

#map[0][0][1]=0
#map[1][0][4]=1
#map[2][0][7]=1
[/code]

See complex specials below.


[h1]'COMPLEX%SPECIALS%'[/h1]

Complex specials first swap out any data surrounded by %% and then surrounded by ' '

For example:
[code]

~pX=%player.x%;
~pY=%player.y%;
~pZ=%player.z%;
#'map[%pX%][%pY%][%pZ%]'=BUNKER ENTRANCE[/code]

Currently it works using temp vars as above not direct calls to player.var or target.var.

You can now specify a delay before the next script action processes. The delay runs until the delay value reaches 0, subtracting 1 each tick. The value can hold any number but bear in mind too high a number will result in too long a delay!

short delay:
[code]delay 100[/code]

long delay:
[code]delay 1000[/code]

[b]START TIMER[/b] - resumes an active timer.
[code]stop timer 0[/code]


[b]STOP TIMER[/b] - pauses an active timer.
[code]stop timer 10[/code]

[b]ERASE TIMER[/b] - deletes an active timer.
[code]erase timer 5[/code]

Timers will need to be micromanaged. The best way would be to create a variable pointer to timers you want to have control over. Timers are incremented from 0 and their data is stored in session_map_data. Type edit session to view.

[code]
#healtimer=1;
start timer %healtimer%[/code]
[/code]


[h1]BUGS FIXED[/h1]

[b]TIMED EVENTS[/b] are now working again!
[code]after x second do something[/code]
[code]every x minutes do something[/code]

[b]DELETE MULTIPLE CHARACTERS[/b]
Delete no longer deletes multiple characters occasionally when pressing backspace.

[b]DELETE KEY:[/b]
no longer deletes entire code entry while text is being rendered, was most notable when adlengine was loading if you made mistakes trying to enter commands and had to delete characters.

notes.title: ADLENGINE v1.1.55.3b NOW LIVE - LETS GET DYNAMIC!
notes.content:
Another big update bringing some cool new functionality to #ADLENGINE that increases both the control you have over the engine and the environments you are creating.

-----------------------------
[h1]NEW %SPECIALS%:[/h1]
-----------------------------

%specials% can be placed in any command or as part of any data and provide a means to LOOKUP data, when processed the engine checks against, vars, map data and more to return the current value of the special.

e.g.

[code[room description is You are standing in a cellar, a grill lies %grillstatus%[/code]

When the room description is rendered %grillstatus% will be swapped with a value you have set up in a variable for example as per below. This happens as it happens.

[code]$grillstatus=open[/code]
[code]grill.if opened $grillstatus=open[/code]
[code]grill.if closed $grillstatus=closed[/code]
------------------------------------------------------------

NEW: Dynamic room name and description: allows you to add %specials% which are processed at rendering, reflecting changes as they happen.

NEW: adlengine will try to load images / sounds from a new game folder in users/username/adlengine/gamename - scripts will follow in a future update.

-------------------------
[h1]NEW VARIABLES:[/h1]

To declare a local variable (accessed only in the same room):
[code]$varname=something[/code]

To declare a global variable (accessed anywhere in the map):
[code]#varname=something[/code]

To declare a private variable (useful for storing things to do with the player):
[code]~varname=something[/code]


[b]VARS against VARS[/b]
Vars can now be used to manipulate (divide,times,minus,plus,equals and append) each other in any combination; As follows:
[code]$varname-anothervar[/code]

---------------------------

----------------------------------------------------------
[h1]NEW CUSTOMISE THEME COMMANDS:[/h1]
----------------------------------------------------------

[b]Currently You Have Access To The Following![/b]
Text Exposed:
[list]
[*]{text-main}
[*]{text-loc}
[*]{text-chat}
[*]{text-debug}
[*]{text-input}
[*]{text-inputmarker}
[/list]

[b]Images Exposed:[/b]
[list]
[*]{image-main}
[*]{image-title}
[*]{image-splash}
[*]{image-inputbg}
[*]{
[/list]

[b]Text Properties:[/b]
[*].x
[*].y
[*].font
[*].fontsize
[*].fontcolor.r
[*].fontcolor.g
[*].fontcolor.b
[*].visible

[b]Image Properties:[/b]
[list]
[*].x
[*].y
[*].width
[*].height
[*].image
[*].opacity
[*].visible
[/list]

To edit a theme element you would do the following:
[code]{text-main}.fontsize=32[/code]

You can also create your own elements by:
[code]{text-name}.new[/code]
[code]{image-name}.new[/code]

To delete a theme element:
[code]{text-name}.delete[/code]

To show / hide a theme element:
[code]{text-name}.visible=1[/code]
[code]{text-name}.visible=0[/code]
---------------------------------------------

-----------------------
[h1]SOUND ENGINE:[/h1]
-----------------------
You can now LOOP / STOP SOUNDS.

To loop a sound:
[code]loop sound soundname[/code]

To stop a sound:
[code]stop sound soundname[/code]
------------------------------------------------

notes.title: Working on Stand-alone Editor
notes.content:
Head down. Busy piecing together the stand-alone editor and will get it to the point where it is IN-GAME. So the next update wont be till its matched.

The new editor is great, syncing beautifully across.

One new bit of functionality (available in the next update) is the goto command now accepts location, such as 0|0|0| which means you could easily map exits to a room not conforming to the grid. For example a secret passage might take you back to the start of the map. OR you might want to teleport the player to a jail cell. That sort of thing.

Character data now syncs correctly without leaving traces of old character location behind as it replaces the location rather than cycling, copying old to new and deleting the old. Alot more efficient and accurate.

The interactable map also has quick toggle exits, which make building your maps quick and easy. It simply fires commands to adlengine to mirror the data across as you make changes. It is pretty much real-time but delays will occur where focus is lost from adlengine as it will pause and catches up when in focus. Fingers crossed this is only due to it being in preview mode.

I will write the ability to quickly add / delete rooms next.

One major speed gain is that I can now live test both the editor and adlengine without exporting it first as I was previously.

I'm open to ideas for what elements of the engine you want exposing in the editor and whether you prefer everything open before you, or if you'd rather show only what you need i.e. toggle between viewing objects, characters, scripts etc.

Or if there is anything that would speed up your development.


While it doesn't look overly pretty it makes creating 100x faster.

I will push the update as soon as I can, once I do I will make the editor available.

notes.title: ADLENGINE PATCH (NOW 1.1.55.2o) - MAJOR EXITS FIX + QUICK MAP EDITOR + EDIT COMMANDS
notes.content:
This update brings a major fix to the exits, which now should work perfectly!

i.e. build exit e

Using the build room command instead of the build exit command will force move you into the new room...


[h1]PLUS - QUICK MAP EDITOR[/h1]

The all new quick map editor / map. To access the map enter the command map or m for short.

[u]In Creative Mode:[/u]

hover over the exit slots and hold ALT + Click Right Mouse Button to toggle exits ON / OFF.

Hold ALT + click Left Mouse Button to toggle an existing exit as OPEN / CLOSED / LOCKED.

Click the Middle Mouse Button over an existing exit to force move in that direction.

[u]In Play Mode:[/u]

Double click Left mouse button over an exit to move in that direction.


[h1]PLUS - NEW EDIT COMMANDS[/h1]

The all new edit commands.

You can now edit the raw data behind your world/game using the following commands:
[code]
edit config[/code]
Allows you to edit settings.

[code]edit session[/code]
Allows you to edit exit data / timed events on the fly.

[code]edit map[/code]
Allows you to quickly tweak / edit the map.

[code]edit scripts[/code]
Allows you to edit scripts that have been stored.

[code]edit custom[/code]
Allows you to edit custom scripts that you've created from using the if command.

[code]edit events[/code]
Allows you to edit event data. Access events timeline using events

[code]edit inv[/code]
Allows you to tweak / edit the players inventory, including equipped and worn items.

[code]edit private[/code]
Allows you to edit any private data.

[code]edit lookup[/code]
Allows you to edit the lookup data.

[code]edit lang[/code]
Allows you to edit the language data.

All changes will be automatically saved every 5 seconds, press the update button to commit the changes and refresh the map (look).

These new commands will help you to make minor tweaks to data rather than always typing out full commands. 

The data format is .json which if you understand the structure you could also add / delete your own data manually.

notes.title: ADLENGINE BUILD 1.1.55.2n... PART 2...
notes.content:
Also in the last update (forgot to mention)...

LOCAL SCRIPTs defined in the .verbase collection file will default their location to X|Y|Z| (off the grid) until they are assigned.

They can be assigned with:
[code]use script scriptname
i.e. use script triggertrap
[/code]

This will then assign a local script of trigger trap in your current location (and only usable / callable at the specified location)

-----------------------------------

NEW COMMAND: Export.

[code]
export entityname
i.e. export gate
[/code]

This command will (in time) automagically work out what type of object you mean, such as room, object or character. It will then export any entity you specify as .verbose script format. It will also store the data in the editor (should you require). Currently it exports objects.

The output will be a list of the descriptive equivalents of the data, e.g.

[code]"0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-OBJ":"NOTE","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-NAME":"Tattered Note","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-DESC":"The note is torn, tattered and soiled.","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISVISIBLE":"n","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISUSEABLE":"y","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISTAKEABLE":"y","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISREADABLE":"y","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-MESSAGE":"It appears to be a poster from some faction. The only words legible; From dust shall we rise. On the back, some one has scrawled DO NOT ENTER THE BUNKER, in what appears to be BLOOD!.","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ID":"NOTE01"[/code]

Will be converted to the following:
[code]build note;
note.name is Tattered Note;
note.description is The note is torn, tattered and soiled.;
note is hidden;
note is usable;
note is takeable;
note is readable;
[/code]

Next update I will also be adding an Edit command that can be used to edit any entity, which will automatically launch the editor with the specified entities data ready for exporting / storing etc.

------------------------------------------

NEW COMMAND: Ignore
[code]ignore any,words,you,want
i.e. ignore the,a
[/code]

This is currently experimental. Be careful what you ignore as it may well break commands. I will be adding in a failsafe for words that form part of a command (so they are not ignored).

Currently, to prevent say; "the" from the word theme being ignored it searches for " the " not "the".

NEW COMMAND: Export.

export entityname
i.e. export gate
[/code]

The output will be a list of the descriptive equivalents of the data, e.g.

[code]"0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-OBJ":"NOTE","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-NAME":"Tattered Note","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-DESC":"The note is torn, tattered and soiled.","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISVISIBLE":"n","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISUSEABLE":"y","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISTAKEABLE":"y","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ISREADABLE":"y","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-MESSAGE":"It appears to be a poster from some faction. The only words legible; From dust shall we rise. On the back, some one has scrawled DO NOT ENTER THE BUNKER, in what appears to be BLOOD!.","0|0|0|OBJ-NOTE-ID":"NOTE01"[/code]

note.description is The note is torn, tattered and soiled.;

note is usable;
note is takeable;
note is readable;

------------------------------------------

[code]ignore any,words,you,want
i.e. ignore the,a
[/code]

This is currently experimental. Be careful what you ignore as it may well break commands. I will be adding in a failsafe for words that form part of a command (so they are not ignored).

Currently, to prevent say; "the" from the word theme being ignored it searches for " the " not "the".

notes.title: ADLENGINE BUILD 1.1.55.2/a NOW LIVE!
notes.content:
Another big update, includes a better example starting level, the fantasy mud from the tutorial. You can launch the old one: load oldgame.adlengine

[h1]BIG CHANGES:[/h1]

You can now buy / sell objects:

A room can be made into a shop:
[code]room is a shop[/code]

OR demoted to a regular room:
[code]room is not a shop[/code]

You need to set an owner of the room:
[code]owner is bob[/code]

To buy or sell an item, the item must have a currency assigned: i.e.
[code]treasure.currency = gold[/code]

And a value given: i.e.
[code]treasure.value = 100[/code]

[b]IF BUYING[/b] you need to have enough of the matching currency.

To Buy:
[code]buy sword[/code]

[b]IF SELLING[/b] the room needs an owner, the owner needs to be in the room and the owner must have enough of the matching currency available to buy it.

To Sell:
[code]sell rope[/code]

When building objects for sale in shops, build them as static objects that cant be taken. i.e.
[code]build sword[/code]
[code]build rope[/code]

This prevents anyone taking them. The player will automatically take the item when its bought.


[h1]IMPORTANT NOTICES:[/h1]

A) when steam updates it will overwrite files in the folder, make sure you keep files backed up elsewhere so you can plug in custom images / sounds etc again.

B) when using the query command it is best practise to use it to call a stored script or simple commands
i.e.
[code]?strength=100:do liftitem!narrate you cant lift it.[/code]

C) when setting parameters of objects first focus on the object, then do the setting i.e.
[code]focus sword
sword.damage = 10[/code]


Also make sure you back up game.adlengine and any other important files or you will lose any progress made.


[h1]NEW COMMANDS:[/h1]

[code]small info[/code]
[code]medium info[/code]
[code]big info[/code]
[code]large info[/code]
Sets the size of the message bar font.

[code]red info[/code]
[code]green info[/code]
[code]blue info[/code]
[code]white info[/code]
[code]black info[/code]
[code]grey info[/code]
Sets the colour of the message bar font.

[code]clear info[/code]
Clears the message bar.

[code]info-1[/code]
Deletes the furthest character from the right of the message bar.

[code]info / info space[/code]
Renders a space to the message bar at the bottom of the screen.

[code]info[/code]
i.e. info You are feeling unwell.
Renders to the message bar at the bottom of the screen.

[code]write / write space[/code]
Renders a space to the text queue.

[code]write[/code]
i.e. write The door slammed shut.
Similar to the Narrate command but doesn't include the ' ' s

[code]clear ticker[/code]
Clears any text currently queued to be rendered.

[code]save[/code]
Saves game data to the hard drive (more user-friendly thand dl)

[h1]FIXES:[/h1]

FIX: typed commands were wiping when commands were being performed, i.e. using event timers.

notes.title: ADLENGINE BUILD 1.1.55.1i... NOW LIVE!
notes.content:
-------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------

WHAT'S NEW?

-------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------

SHOWDATA:

show / hide data for the game...
[code]showdata[/code]

-------------------------------------------------

IN-GAME SCRIPT EDITOR:

Launch using:
[code].editor[/code]

Scripts can be exported, stored as a local script (only works in that location) OR global (works anywhere)

all script entries must be terminated with ;

to run stored scripts use the do command which matches the name of the script. you can also import .verbose scripts into the editor (allowing external creation) using the file choose dialog.

you can also start / stop scripts (which enables / disables them)

[code]stop scriptname[/code]
[code]start scriptname[/code]

-------------------------------------------------

[h1]YOU CAN NOW SET VARIABLES:[/h1]

Variables can be set to numbers, strings, other variables, object / player / target properties... for example..

[code]#boo=100[/code]
[code]#boo=baa[/code]
[code]#boo=player.health[/code]
[code]#boo=orc.health[/code]
[code]#boo=target.strength[/code]

-------------------------------------------------

[h1]AND MANIPULATE THEM:[/h1]

[code]#baa=10[/code]

[b]Minusing:[/b]
[code]#boo-baa[/code]
[code]#boo-10[/code]

[b]Dividing:[/b]
[code]#boo/baa[/code]
[code]#boo/10[/code]

[b]Multiplying:[/b]
[code]#boo*baa[/code]
[code]#boo*100[/code]

[b]Adding:[/b]
[code]#boo+baa[/code]
[code]#boo+50[/code]

[b]Appending (stringing sentences together)[/b]
[code]#boo=hello
#baa=there
#boo&baa[/code]

[i]Result: hello there[/i]

-------------------------------------------------

[h1]QUERYING VARIABLES[/h1]

[b]Equal To:[/b]
[code]random 1xd6
#rolled=random
?rolled=1:narrate you escaped!narrate you were caught[/code]

[i]the : indicates what to do if TRUE, ! indicates FALSE. IF you dont put anything for either of these two values it wont do anything, but both must be present...

For example:
[code]?rolled=1:narrate you escaped!narrate you were caught [BOTH ACTIVE][/code]
[code]?rolled=1:narrate you escaped! [TRUE ONLY][/code]
[code]?rolled=1:!narrate you escaped [FALSE ONLY][/code]
[code]?rolled=0:! [NULL][/code]

[b]Less Than:[/b]
[code]#isalive=target.health
?isalive<1:narrate it died![/code]

[b]More Than:[/b]
[code]random 2xd6
#rolled=random
?rolled>4:narrate you scaled the ladder!narrate the ladder broke under your feet[/code]

[b]Not Equal To:[/b]
[code]random 2xd6
#rolled=random
?rolledx12:narrate nothing happened!you triggered the trap[/code]

-------------------------------------------------

[h1]ROLLING DICE[/h1]

The random command can be used to roll a number of dice. The 1 below indicates the number of dice, which could be any number. The 6 below indicates the number of sides on each dice.

[code]random 1xd6[/code]
[code]random 2xd20[/code]

Once you have rolled the dice, the rolled value can be stored in a variable for further use / querying.

i.e.

[code]#rolled=random[/code]
[code]#strengthtest=random[/code]

You can then use this variable in setting / querying properties and more.

[h1]RANDOM CHOICE[/h1]

The random choice command allows you to choose between a set number of strings / numbers i.e. you can specify up to 16 values currently.

[code]choose 1,2,3,4,5,6[/code]

or [code]choose a,b,c,d,e,f[/code]

For example: you could choose a random encounter.

[code]choose rat,goblin,orc,mummy[/code]

or choose a random sentence of a similar nature to vary the text... i.e.

[code]choose you disarm the trap,you disable the trap, your expertise cancels out the trap.[/code]

You can then set this to a variable:
[code]#result=chosen[/code]

Then you can either narrate it, append it, or query it.

You CAN also set commands to choose from i.e.

[code]choose look, force n, drop skull[/code]

-------------------------------------------------

[h1]SETTING OBJECT PROPERTIES:[/h1]
[code]gun.ammo=10[/code]

-------------------------------------------------

[h1]SETTING PROPERTIES OF "YOUR" PLAYER:[/h1]
[code]player.health=100[/code]

-------------------------------------------------

[h1]SETTING PROPERTIES OF "OTHER" CHARS / OBJECTS:[/h1]
[code]focus orc
target.health=100 (or) orc.health=100[/code]

IF a property doesn't exist it will be created.

[i]target orc is used when playing to target a specific creature to attack
focus orc is used in scripting... (no feedback - just points to the object you want to focus certain scripting commands on)[/i]

-------------------------------------------------

Lets say we want to attack an orc and have it receive damage.

[code]focus orc
random 1xd6
#dam=random
target.healh-dam
?dam=6:narrate you score a critical hit![/code]

-------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------

BUG FIXES / AMENDS:

-------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------

NEW COMMAND: object is unequipable / object is not unequipable
NEW COMMAND: object is readable / object is not readable
FIX: help command now launches manual in a new browser window!
FIX: narrate command now accepts variables. i.e. narrate health
FIX: player data moves with the player
FIX: blank entries for specific commands i.e. drop are no longer processed and return "you can't drop that" etc..
FIX: custom commands can no longer be called outside of creative mode.
FIX: removed debug feedback for query (?) command
FIX: start.verbose is now present (now detectable) - place anything in here you want to run when the engine has finished launching.

-------------------------------------------------

~ Liam

[code]random 1xd6[/code]
[code]random 2xd20[/code]

[code]#rolled=random[/code]

The random choice command allows you to choose between a set number of strings / numbers i.e. you can specify up to 16 values currently.

[code]choose 1,2,3,4,5,6[/code]

notes.title: Creating MUDs in ADLENGINE...
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

There's quite a few people asking about using ADLENGINE to build MUDs. It is totally possible to build a MUD in adliberum engine, especially with recent updates including the ability to roll dice and with the addition of variables / pointers.

I will be running a tutorial series on how this could be achieved shortly. The biggest thing holding the engine back is AI / NPC. Which is being worked on in the background.

Here's a brief insight:

For example you can create any stat you wish for example on your character player.health=100 for example. You can then write scripts that manipulate the values (-+/*) and query against example for when a monster perishes etc. 

Here's a quick look at variables..

setting:
[code]#damage=0;[/code]

minus:
[code]#health-damage;[/code]

plus:
[code]#health+healing;[/code]

divide:
[code]#maxhealth/poison;[/code]

multiply:
[code]#maxhealth*level;[/code]

append:
[code]#stringa&stringb;[/code]

creating pointers:
[code]#playerhealth=player.health;[/code]

Targeting:
[code]focus orc;
target.health-10;[/code]

Damage:
[code]player.health-10;[/code]

Querying:
[code]player.strength=12;
player.health=100;

#playerstrength=player.strength;
#playerhealth=player.health;

?playerstrength>12:do something!do something else;
?playerhealth<1:playerdied!;[/code]

Factoring Stats:
[code]random 1xd6;
#rolled=random;
?rolled=1:disarmtrap!setofftrap;[/code]


Shout if you get stuck or have suggestions / requests, as I may be able to help with workarounds / scripts / additional commands in the mean time.

~ Liam

notes.title: VARIABLES ARE COMING...
notes.content:
Alongside working on the Scifi Kit and getting the core NPC / AI systems in place I am now adding the ability to set CREATE, SET, FETCH, ADD TO, SUBTRACT FROM, TIMES BY, DIVIDE BY and most importantly COMPARE against.

As variables are deemed more advanced commands, the command entry gets a little more complex. (I will implement verbose versions of these commands once they are fully implemented, tested and working)...

Let's look at how you will use these new powerful commands, when ready.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Variables can be of three types. They are by default global.

private. only held and accessible on YOUR machine.
local. only held and accessible at a certain location (across multiplayer)
global. accessible anywhere (across multiplayer)

[h1]SET VARIABLE[/h1]
[code]#health=100[/code]

[h1]SET VARIABLE[/h1]
[code]#health=100[/code]

[h1]ADD TO VARIABLE (NUMBERS)[/h1]
[code]#health=health+1[/code]

[h1]ADD TO VARIABLE (TEXT)[/h1]
[code]#glyph=fire
#rune=ball
#spell=glyph+rune[/code]

[h1]SUBTRACT FROM (NUMBER / VARIABLE)[/h1]
[code]#health=health-1[/code]

[h1]MULTIPLY BY (NUMBER / VARIABLE)[/h1]
[code]#xp=0
#level=10
#xpearned=5
#xp=xpearned*level[/code]

[h1]DIVIDE BY (NUMBER / VARIABLE)[/h1]
[code]#health=100
#health=health/2[/code]

[h1]IF / ELSE[/h1]
[code]?health<=0:gameover=y!gameover=n[/code]

The above code checks if the players health is less than or equal (<=) to 0 and then (:) game is over ELSE (!) not game over

You can also run scripts / run script commands in the IF / ELSE i.e.
[code]?health<=100:health=health+1!health=100[/code]

All of  the above commands can be used in scripting commands and in .verbose script files.

As these ifs allow a singular event IF TRUE / FALSE you could also combine with a custom command.

if gameover then do this and do that

OR for even more power, SET or use VARIABLE / IF ELSE inside custom commands.


--------------- [h1]EXAMPLE[/h1] --------------------

An example of how they might be used..

In the bunker demo there is a gate. We want to allow the player to scale the gate if they have a high acrobatics level.

[code]#acrobatics=0[/code]

[code]if climb gate then ?acrobatics=10:climbovergate!narrate You cant climb it[/code]

[code]if climbovergate then force n and narrate You scale the gate[/code]

To be able to climb the gate the acrobats variable would need to match 10, otherwise they will fail. You could increase their acrobatics level when they complete training for example.

[code]if learnacrobats then #acrobats+1[/code]

Lets say they learn it by reading books on acrobatics.

[code]if acrobaticsweekly.read then #acrobatics+1[/code]

[quote]force *direction* is a new set of commands which will also be added in the next update allowing you to move the player regardless of locked doors etc (where needed) great for letting the player find other ways to exit etc.

i.e. force s[/quote]


------------------------------------------------

Variables should be coming in the next update.

~ Liam

notes.title: TUTORIAL - BUILDING A WORKING LIGHT SWITCH
notes.content:
One of the coolest things about adlengine is the ability to use its integrated descriptive scripting language. Designed to be simple to use yet powerful enough to handle complex requirements.

I will be looking at ways to make the scripting easier and soon you will be able to check if certain conditions are met, such as if skull=open then...

Once you have written a .verbose script you can use it again and again. My aim is to have collections of scripts available in a multitude of themes to allow quick world / scenario building.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Take for example... CREATING A WORKING LIGHT & SWITCH...

[i]you can download the .verbose file at https://www.adliberum.com/engine/scripts/ - just plug it into the folder and use the command "run build light" (available in build 1.1.54.8)

to import your own .verbose files after enabling creative mode... double click the top right of the screen, click the second file dialog button down and locate the .verbose file you wish to import on your computer.

.verbose files can be edited in notepad, notepad++ or other text editor[/i]

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// first enable creative mode...
[code].creative[/code]

[h1]
----------------------------------
LEVEL 1 SCRIPTING
----------------------------------
[/h1]

// lets build a light...
build light

... and a switch to control it... //
build switch

// add some commands to control the light using the light switch.
[code]
if turn on switch then narrate the light came on. and room is well lit;
if turn off switch then narrate the light went out. and room is barely lit;
[/code]

[h1]
----------------------------------
LEVEL 2 SCRIPTING
----------------------------------
[/h1]

// update the description based on the lights state...
[code]if room is well lit then light.description is the light shines brightly
if room is barely lit then light.description is the light is off[/code]

Finally lets capture a few variations on how people might interact with the switch.
[code]
turn on light==turn on switch
turn off light==turn off switch
turn light on==turn on switch
turn light off==turn off switch
turn switch on==turn on switch
turn switch off==turn off switch
[/code]

[h1]
----------------------------------
LEVEL 3 SCRIPTING
----------------------------------
[/h1]

[code]build bulb[/code]

// lets make it part of the light.
[code]
bulb.is inside light
[/code]

// lets make it easier to interact with the object by allowing a shorter name variation.
[code]
lightbulb==bulb
[/code]

// let's stop the switch from working...
[code]
if delete lightbulb then disable switch and room is barely lit
if disable switch then turn switch off==switch is broken and turn switch on==switch is broken
if switch is broken then narrate nothing happens.
[/code]

// prevent the player putting another bulb in the light
[code]if put bulb inside light then narrate There's already a bulb.[/code]

[h1]
----------------------------------
LEVEL 4 SCRIPTING
----------------------------------
[/h1]

// allow the player to smash the bulb
[code]
if smash bulb then delete bulb and narrate darkness spills glass into the room.
if delete bulb then bulb is gone and if put bulb inside light then reset switch and reset light
if bulb is gone then room is barely lit and disable switch
[/code]

// make the light go out if the bulb is taken / smashed
[code]
if lights out then no bulb and light goes out
if light goes out then turn off switch==switch is broken and turn on switch==switch is broken
[/code]


// make the bulb hot when on
[code]
if turn on switch then bulb is hot
if turn off switch then bulb is hot
if bulb is hot then narrate Ouch!
[/code]

[h1]
----------------------------------
LEVEL 5 SCRIPTING
----------------------------------
[/h1]

// disable the switch if the bulb is broken or taken out!
[code]
if disable switch then turn off switch==switch is broken and turn on switch==switch is broken

if switch is broken then narrate nothing happens.
[/code]

// allow the player to take the bulb out
[code]
bulb.if taken no bulb
[/code]

// turn off the light if the bulb is smashed OR taken out
[code]
if no bulb then room is barely lit and reset light script
[/code]

// reset the switch IF the player puts in a new bulb
[code]
if reset switch then if turn on switch then narrate the light came on. and if turn off switch then narrate the light went out.
[/code]

// reset the light if a new bulb is put in
[code]
if reset light then room is well lit and let there be light
[/code]

// and allow them to put a new bulb in
[code]
if reset light script then if put bulb inside light then reset switch

if let there be light then if turn on switch then narrate the light came on. and if turn off switch then narrate the light went out.
[/code]

notes.title: Adliberum Engine 1.1.54.5 now live!
notes.content:
v1.1.54.5 brings us custom sounds.

Sounds can be imported by renaming the package.nw file to package.zip
placing the files inside the zip and renaming it back to package.nw.

To be able to play sounds you need the sounds you want to be able to play in both .ogg and m4a format.

Sounds that match the same name as main commands inside the zip will be played when the sound is successful, for example...

[code]open.ogg
open.m4a
close.ogg
close.m4a
wear.ogg
wear.m4a
take.ogg
take.m4a
[/code]

if the command is successful it will play the sound.

To play a custom sound you can also use scripting to play a sound. This could also be placed inside a .verbose script file. If the sound is not found it won't play it.

e.g.

[code]gate.if unlocked play sound metalgate[/code]

You can also place them within a folder inside the zip.

Then you would just need to include the folder name in front

e.g.

[code]gate.if unlocked play sound fx\metalgate[/code]

~ Liam
